paragraphs.text: Would that ye could bear with me in a little foolishness: but indeed ye do bear with me.
paragraphs.original: Ὄφελον ἀνείχεσθέ μου μικρόν τι ἀφροσύνης· ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀνέχεσθέ μου.
paragraphs.translit: Ophelon aneichesthe mou mikron ti aphrosynēs· alla kai anechesthe mou.

paragraphs.text: For I am jealous over you with a godly jealousy: for I espoused you to one husband, that I might present you [as] a pure virgin to Christ.
paragraphs.original: ζηλῶ γὰρ ὑμᾶς θεοῦ ζήλῳ, ἡρμοσάμην γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἑνὶ ἀνδρὶ παρθένον ἁγνὴν παραστῆσαι τῷ Χριστῷ·
paragraphs.translit: zēlō gar hymas theou zēlō, hērmosamēn gar hymas heni andri parthenon hagnēn parastēsai tō Christō·

paragraphs.text: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve in his craftiness, your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity and the purity that is toward Christ.
paragraphs.original: φοβοῦμαι δὲ μή πως, ὡς ὁ ὄφις ἐξηπάτησεν Εὕαν ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτοῦ, φθαρῇ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἁπλότητος καὶ τῆς ἁγνότητος τῆς εἰς τὸν Χριστόν.
paragraphs.translit: phoboumai de mē pōs, hōs ho ophis exēpatēsen Heuan en tē panourgia autou, phtharē ta noēmata hymōn apo tēs haplotētos kai tēs hagnotētos tēs eis ton Christon.

paragraphs.text: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or [if] ye receive a different spirit, which ye did not receive, or a different gospel, which ye did not accept, ye do well to bear with [him].
paragraphs.original: εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἄλλον Ἰησοῦν κηρύσσει ὃν οὐκ ἐκηρύξαμεν, ἢ πνεῦμα ἕτερον λαμβάνετε ὃ οὐκ ἐλάβετε, ἢ εὐαγγέλιον ἕτερον ὃ οὐκ ἐδέξασθε, καλῶς ἀνέχεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: ei men gar ho erchomenos allon Iēsoun kēryssei hon ouk ekēryxamen, ē pneuma heteron lambanete ho ouk elabete, ē euangelion heteron ho ouk edexasthe, kalōs anechesthe.

paragraphs.text: For I reckon that I am not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.
paragraphs.original: λογίζομαι γὰρ μηδὲν ὑστερηκέναι τῶν ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων·
paragraphs.translit: logizomai gar mēden hysterēkenai tōn hyperlian apostolōn·

paragraphs.text: But though [I be] rude in speech, yet [am I] not in knowledge; nay, in every way have we made [this] manifest unto you in all things.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἰδιώτης τῷ λόγῳ, ἀλλʼ οὐ τῇ γνώσει, ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ φανερώσαντες ἐν πᾶσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: ei de kai idiōtēs tō logō, allʼ ou tē gnōsei, allʼ en panti phanerōsantes en pasin eis hymas.

paragraphs.text: Or did I commit a sin in abasing myself that ye might be exalted, because I preached to you the gospel of God for nought?
paragraphs.original: Ἢ ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησα ἐμαυτὸν ταπεινῶν ἵνα ὑμεῖς ὑψωθῆτε, ὅτι δωρεὰν τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγέλιον εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν;
paragraphs.translit: Ē hamartian epoiēsa emauton tapeinōn hina hymeis hypsōthēte, hoti dōrean to tou theou euangelion euēngelisamēn hymin;

paragraphs.text: I robbed other churches, taking wages [of them] that I might minister unto you;
paragraphs.original: ἄλλας ἐκκλησίας ἐσύλησα λαβὼν ὀψώνιον πρὸς τὴν ὑμῶν διακονίαν,
paragraphs.translit: allas ekklēsias esylēsa labōn opsōnion pros tēn hymōn diakonian,

paragraphs.text: and when I was present with you and was in want, I was not a burden on any man; for the brethren, when they came from Macedonia, supplied the measure of my want; and in everything I kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and [so] will I keep [myself].
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑστερηθεὶς οὐ κατενάρκησα οὐθενός· τὸ γὰρ ὑστέρημά μου προσανεπλήρωσαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας· καὶ ἐν παντὶ ἀβαρῆ ἐμαυτὸν ὑμῖν ἐτήρησα καὶ τηρήσω.
paragraphs.translit: kai parōn pros hymas kai hysterētheis ou katenarkēsa outhenos· to gar hysterēma mou prosaneplērōsan hoi adelphoi elthontes apo Makedonias· kai en panti abarē emauton hymin etērēsa kai tērēsō.

paragraphs.text: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this glorying in the regions of Achaia.
paragraphs.original: ἔστιν ἀλήθεια Χριστοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ ὅτι ἡ καύχησις αὕτη οὐ φραγήσεται εἰς ἐμὲ ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τῆς Ἀχαΐας.
paragraphs.translit: estin alētheia Christou en emoi hoti hē kauchēsis hautē ou phragēsetai eis eme en tois klimasi tēs Achaias.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore? because I love you not? God knoweth.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τί; ὅτι οὐκ ἀγαπῶ ὑμᾶς; ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν.
paragraphs.translit: dia ti; hoti ouk agapō hymas; ho theos oiden.

paragraphs.text: But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them that desire an occasion; that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we.
paragraphs.original: Ὃ δὲ ποιῶ καὶ ποιήσω, ἵνα ἐκκόψω τὴν ἀφορμὴν τῶν θελόντων ἀφορμήν, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ καυχῶνται εὑρεθῶσιν καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς.
paragraphs.translit: Ho de poiō kai poiēsō, hina ekkopsō tēn aphormēn tōn thelontōn aphormēn, hina en hō kauchōntai heurethōsin kathōs kai hēmeis.

paragraphs.text: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, fashioning themselves into apostles of Christ.
paragraphs.original: οἱ γὰρ τοιοῦτοι ψευδαπόστολοι, ἐργάται δόλιοι, μετασχηματιζόμενοι εἰς ἀποστόλους Χριστοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hoi gar toioutoi pseudapostoloi, ergatai dolioi, metaschēmatizomenoi eis apostolous Christou·

paragraphs.text: And no marvel; for even Satan fashioneth himself into an angel of light.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐ θαῦμα, αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Σατανᾶς μετασχηματίζεται εἰς ἄγγελον φωτός·
paragraphs.translit: kai ou thauma, autos gar ho Satanas metaschēmatizetai eis angelon phōtos·

paragraphs.text: It is no great thing therefore if his ministers also fashion themselves as ministers of righteousness, whose end shall be according to their works.
paragraphs.original: οὐ μέγα οὖν εἰ καὶ οἱ διάκονοι αὐτοῦ μετασχηματίζονται ὡς διάκονοι δικαιοσύνης, ὧν τὸ τέλος ἔσται κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ou mega oun ei kai hoi diakonoi autou metaschēmatizontai hōs diakonoi dikaiosynēs, hōn to telos estai kata ta erga autōn.

paragraphs.text: I say again, let no man think me foolish; but if [ye do], yet as foolish receive me, that I also may glory a little.
paragraphs.original: Πάλιν λέγω, μή τίς με δόξῃ ἄφρονα εἶναι— εἰ δὲ μή γε, κἂν ὡς ἄφρονα δέξασθέ με, ἵνα κἀγὼ μικρόν τι καυχήσωμαι·
paragraphs.translit: Palin legō, mē tis me doxē aphrona einai— ei de mē ge, kan hōs aphrona dexasthe me, hina kagō mikron ti kauchēsōmai·

paragraphs.text: That which I speak, I speak not after the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of glorying.
paragraphs.original: ὃ λαλῶ οὐ κατὰ κύριον λαλῶ, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ, ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ ὑποστάσει τῆς καυχήσεως.
paragraphs.translit: ho lalō ou kata kyrion lalō, allʼ hōs en aphrosynē, en tautē tē hypostasei tēs kauchēseōs.

paragraphs.text: Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.
paragraphs.original: ἐπεὶ πολλοὶ καυχῶνται κατὰ σάρκα, κἀγὼ καυχήσομαι.
paragraphs.translit: epei polloi kauchōntai kata sarka, kagō kauchēsomai.

paragraphs.text: For ye bear with the foolish gladly, being wise [yourselves].
paragraphs.original: ἡδέως γὰρ ἀνέχεσθε τῶν ἀφρόνων φρόνιμοι ὄντες·
paragraphs.translit: hēdeōs gar anechesthe tōn aphronōn phronimoi ontes·

paragraphs.text: For ye bear with a man, if he bringeth you into bondage, if he devoureth you, if he taketh you [captive], if he exalteth himself, if he smiteth you on the face.
paragraphs.original: ἀνέχεσθε γὰρ εἴ τις ὑμᾶς καταδουλοῖ, εἴ τις κατεσθίει, εἴ τις λαμβάνει, εἴ τις ἐπαίρεται, εἴ τις εἰς πρόσωπον ὑμᾶς δέρει.
paragraphs.translit: anechesthe gar ei tis hymas katadouloi, ei tis katesthiei, ei tis lambanei, ei tis epairetai, ei tis eis prosōpon hymas derei.

paragraphs.text: I speak by way of disparagement, as though we had been weak. Yet whereinsoever any is bold (I speak in foolishness), I am bold also.
paragraphs.original: κατὰ ἀτιμίαν λέγω, ὡς ὅτι ἡμεῖς ἠσθενήκαμεν· ἐν ᾧ δʼ ἄν τις τολμᾷ, ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ λέγω, τολμῶ κἀγώ.
paragraphs.translit: kata atimian legō, hōs hoti hēmeis ēsthenēkamen· en hō dʼ an tis tolma, en aphrosynē legō, tolmō kagō.

paragraphs.text: Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.
paragraphs.original: Ἑβραῖοί εἰσιν; κἀγώ. Ἰσραηλῖταί εἰσιν; κἀγώ. σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ εἰσιν; κἀγώ.
paragraphs.translit: Hebraioi eisin; kagō. Israēlitai eisin; kagō. sperma Abraam eisin; kagō.

paragraphs.text: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as one beside himself) I more; in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, in deaths oft.
paragraphs.original: διάκονοι Χριστοῦ εἰσιν; παραφρονῶν λαλῶ, ὑπὲρ ἐγώ· ἐν κόποις περισσοτέρως, ἐν φυλακαῖς περισσοτέρως, ἐν πληγαῖς ὑπερβαλλόντως, ἐν θανάτοις πολλάκις·
paragraphs.translit: diakonoi Christou eisin; paraphronōn lalō, hyper egō· en kopois perissoterōs, en phylakais perissoterōs, en plēgais hyperballontōs, en thanatois pollakis·

paragraphs.text: Of the Jews five times received I forty [stripes] save one.
paragraphs.original: ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων πεντάκις τεσσεράκοντα παρὰ μίαν ἔλαβον,
paragraphs.translit: hypo Ioudaiōn pentakis tesserakonta para mian elabon,

paragraphs.text: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day have I been in the deep;
paragraphs.original: τρὶς ἐραβδίσθην, ἅπαξ ἐλιθάσθην, τρὶς ἐναυάγησα, νυχθήμερον ἐν τῷ βυθῷ πεποίηκα·
paragraphs.translit: tris erabdisthēn, hapax elithasthēn, tris enauagēsa, nychthēmeron en tō bythō pepoiēka·

paragraphs.text: [in] journeyings often, [in] perils of rivers, [in] perils of robbers, [in] perils from [my] countrymen, [in] perils from the Gentiles, [in] perils in the city, [in] perils in the wilderness, [in] perils in the sea, [in] perils among false brethren;
paragraphs.original: ὁδοιπορίαις πολλάκις, κινδύνοις ποταμῶν, κινδύνοις λῃστῶν, κινδύνοις ἐκ γένους, κινδύνοις ἐξ ἐθνῶν, κινδύνοις ἐν πόλει, κινδύνοις ἐν ἐρημίᾳ, κινδύνοις ἐν θαλάσσῃ, κινδύνοις ἐν ψευδαδέλφοις,
paragraphs.translit: hodoiporiais pollakis, kindynois potamōn, kindynois lēstōn, kindynois ek genous, kindynois ex ethnōn, kindynois en polei, kindynois en erēmia, kindynois en thalassē, kindynois en pseudadelphois,

paragraphs.text: [in] labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
paragraphs.original: κόπῳ καὶ μόχθῳ, ἐν ἀγρυπνίαις πολλάκις, ἐν λιμῷ καὶ δίψει, ἐν νηστείαις πολλάκις, ἐν ψύχει καὶ γυμνότητι·
paragraphs.translit: kopō kai mochthō, en agrypniais pollakis, en limō kai dipsei, en nēsteiais pollakis, en psychei kai gymnotēti·

paragraphs.text: Besides those things that are without, there is that which presseth upon me daily, anxiety for all the churches.
paragraphs.original: χωρὶς τῶν παρεκτὸς ἡ ἐπίστασίς μοι ἡ καθʼ ἡμέραν, ἡ μέριμνα πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν.
paragraphs.translit: chōris tōn parektos hē epistasis moi hē kathʼ hēmeran, hē merimna pasōn tōn ekklēsiōn.

paragraphs.text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is caused to stumble, and I burn not?
paragraphs.original: τίς ἀσθενεῖ, καὶ οὐκ ἀσθενῶ; τίς σκανδαλίζεται καὶ οὐκ ἐγὼ πυροῦμαι;
paragraphs.translit: tis asthenei, kai ouk asthenō; tis skandalizetai kai ouk egō pyroumai;

paragraphs.text: If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things that concern my weakness.
paragraphs.original: Εἰ καυχᾶσθαι δεῖ, τὰ τῆς ἀσθενείας μου καυχήσομαι.
paragraphs.translit: Ei kauchasthai dei, ta tēs astheneias mou kauchēsomai.

paragraphs.text: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, he who is blessed for evermore knoweth that I lie not.
paragraphs.original: ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ οἶδεν, ὁ ὢν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι.
paragraphs.translit: ho theos kai patēr tou kyriou Iēsou oiden, ho ōn eulogētos eis tous aiōnas, hoti ou pseudomai.

paragraphs.text: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king guarded the city of the Damascenes in order to take me:
paragraphs.original: ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὁ ἐθνάρχης Ἁρέτα τοῦ βασιλέως ἐφρούρει τὴν πόλιν Δαμασκηνῶν πιάσαι με,
paragraphs.translit: en Damaskō ho ethnarchēs Hareta tou basileōs ephrourei tēn polin Damaskēnōn piasai me,

paragraphs.text: and through a window was I let down in a basket by the wall, and escaped his hands.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διὰ θυρίδος ἐν σαργάνῃ ἐχαλάσθην διὰ τοῦ τείχους καὶ ἐξέφυγον τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai dia thyridos en sarganē echalasthēn dia tou teichous kai exephygon tas cheiras autou.
